All British-Built Ariel Atom and Nomad Vehicles Are Now Available in the U.S.
64 photos
Photo: Ariel
British carmaker Ariel is not exactly mainstream, but that doesn't mean it doesn't have a fair share of fans – not only in the home market, but also across the pond, in the U.S.. Whereas up until now customers there were treated to vehicles made under a licensed manufacturing program, Ariel vehicles will from now on land stateside right off the Brits’ assembly facility.
The company announced this week that, as of now, American customers get access to all four British-built models for the first time, namely the Atom 4 , Atom 4R, Arom 4RR and Nomad 2. Tasked with getting these rides into the proper hands is Arizona-based Forman Motorworks, which has been in bed with Ariel for a long time already.
We're told the first two demonstrator models designed for the American market, an Atom 4 and a 4R, are already being assembled, and they should reach the U.S. in the first quarter of next year. Customer deliveries are expected to begin in the summer of 2027.
The America-spec vehicles are already listed on Forman Motorworks' configurator , so we can form a pretty decent idea of what to expect. Spoiler alert: things are not at all different from what Ariel offers elsewhere, and the prices are quite high.
The Atom 4 in its most basic incarnation uses a Honda -sourced 2.0-liter turbocharged i-VTEC engine that's rated at 345 hp and 310 lb-ft of torque. Those are incredible numbers, if you take into account the fact that this thing weighs just 1,350 pounds (612 kg). The cost of the package: $117,000.
The Atom 4R is basically the same vehicle, but with a significant increase in power levels. That would be 395 horsepower and 369 lb-ft of torque coming from the engine, which are offered to customers for an impressive $166,500.
The third Atom in the lineup, the 4RR, not only throws in an extra consonant, but also 518 horsepower and 405 lb-ft of torque. All of that, plus an engine that revs at a maximum of 8,200 rpm, can be had for yet-to-be-specified prices, but certainly higher than when it comes to the vehicle's siblings.
We expect the sticker to read something along the lines of $280,000, and that's in part owed to the fact that this is the fastest and most powerful Atom made to date.
Finally, the Nomad 2 , the only off-road-oriented vehicle in the lineup, throws in 300 horsepower and nine inches (23 cm) of ground clearance, so that it can easily navigate rough terrain. The price sticker for this one stands at $124,400.
As a reminder, all Ariel vehicles are highly customizable, and they can also be had as rolling chassis. This basically means that every Ariel out there can take a form of its own, within a certain set of approved parts, including engines and transmissions.
